title: Operator Quickpeek: Span Rollup and Proactive Filters
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory doc describing an "operator quickpeek" concept: a compact, actionable trace card for high-volume customers that surface span rollups, inferred root causes, and proactive filter suggestions so on-call and SREs can make decisions faster without opening the full trace waterfall. This is a product + ops playbook and a preliminary wireframe sketch for grooming.

TL;DR:
- Add a compact trace preview UI reachable from trace list and alerts (hover / quick-open).
- Show span rollups (grouped by service/function) with aggregate metrics (p50/p95, error rate) and a small sparkline.
- Provide proactive filter suggestions derived from top contributing spans and anomalous tags (eg: high-latency DB calls, 5xx counts, region).
- Allow one-click expansion to full waterfall or to open a focused explorer with pre-applied filters.

Goals and success metrics (initial):
- Reduce mean time to triage for high-frequency alerts by 30% (measured via incident timeline).
- Decrease number of full-trace opens per alert by 40% for top customers.
- Increase adoption of pre-applied filters from alert sidecars (target 20% of alert actions).

Constraints we must consider:
- Quickpeek must load within 200ms after clicking from trace list for hosted customers.
- Should not materialize full payload (use sampled aggregation + prefix cache).
- Works with model/variant fallbacks; UI should indicate if metrics are approximate (sampling).

Interaction patterns (sketch ideas):
1) Hover quickpeek (desktop): small card anchored to trace row. Card sections: header (trace-id, status, duration), rollup lanes (service groups), top contributors, suggested filters, quick actions.
2) Click quickpeek to open overlay: larger preview with mini-waterfall (no full span rows, just grouped bars), timeline scrubber, and action buttons: "Apply filters & explore", "Open full trace", "Create quick note".
3) Mobile: tap opens stacked full preview; keep interactions conservative.

Key components (details):
- Rollup lane: label (service name), aggregated p50/p95, error %, avg spans/sec, small horizontal bar showing relative latency contribution. Each lane is clickable to expand to service-level spans.
- Top contributor list: top 3 span types (eg. db.query, auth.check, serialization) with delta vs baseline. Click to add filter.
- Proactive filters: inferred from heuristics: high-latency spans, elevated error tags, unusual tag values (region, client_version). Provide confidence score and short rationale.

ASCII wireframe (very rough):
[Quickpeek Card] width ~ 600px
-------------------------------------------------------------
| trace: 0f3a2b (ERR) | 1.2s | p95: 2.8s | sampled: 12/200   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| Services:                                                   |
| [auth     ] ▒▒▒▒▒▒▒  p50 120ms p95 480ms err 0.8%  sparkline |
| [db-read  ] ▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒ p50 350ms p95 1.4s err 2.4%            |
| [serializer] ▒▒▒▒    p50 80ms  p95 140ms err 0.0%           |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| Top contributors: db.query (+370ms), cache.miss (+120ms)     |
| Suggested filters: region=eu-west (conf 0.86)  db.statement=slow (conf 0.71)|
| Actions: [Apply filters & explore] [Open full trace] [Copy id]|
-------------------------------------------------------------

Filtering UX notes:
- Suggested filters should be additive and shown with a short rationale chip (icon + text). Chips can be toggled on/off before applying.
- If user toggles a filter that would reduce results to < 5 traces, show badge "low match" and allow force-apply.
- Preserve user's active global filters when applying quickpeek suggestions; show combined preview count.

Backend / data assumptions:
- Need a lightweight aggregated view API: /traces/preview?trace_id=&context=quickpeek that returns rollup buckets, top contributors, suggested filter candidates, and estimated match count.
- Aggregation TTL: 30s for live traffic; backend computes deltas vs a 1h baseline for anomaly scoring.
- Cache results keyed by trace_id + sampling_token so repeated hovers don't re-run heavy queries.

Open questions / decisions to groom:
- Q1: Where to store suggested filter heuristics? Server-side rules, client-side heuristics, or hybrid? (Pros/cons inlined below)
- Q2: How to signal sampling vs full data to users? Minimal noise, maybe a small "approx" tag and tooltip.
- Q3: Access control for private deployments: should quickpeek fetch local-only metadata? (Probably: respect RBAC and VPC boundaries).

Heuristic options (short):
- Server-rule engine: central source, consistent across clients, easier to A/B, but needs deploy.
- Client heuristics: fast experiment loop but inconsistent and leaking of logic.
- Hybrid: server scores candidates, client ranks and formats suggestions. Recommended: hybrid.

Backlog / groomed tickets (draft):
- PCON-920: quickpeek API prototype (backend aggregation endpoint). (owner: Kenji)
- PCON-921: quickpeek frontend component + hover card (owner: Jordan).
- PCON-922: suggested filters scorer (RND baseline logic) + QA harness (owner: Marta).
- PCON-923: telemetry + SLO for quickpeek latency and accuracy (owner: SRE).
- UX-ALERT-71: accessibility pass (keyboard / screen reader).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Quickpeek card appears on hover/click for trace rows in list with <200ms median render after API response.
- Card shows at least 3 rollup lanes, top contributors, and up to 4 suggested filters with confidence scores.
- "Apply filters & explore" opens explorer with filters applied and correct count.
- Respect RBAC and sampling indicators present.

Edge cases and mitigation:
- Low-sampled traces: show a warning and degrade to "top spans only" mode.
- High-cardinality tags: limit suggestions to tags with stable top-k frequency; add an "advanced" toggle for more.
- Very wide traces with many services: cap rollup lanes to top 8 contributors and show "+N more".

Experiment ideas (post-MVP):
- A/B: surface proactive filter suggestions in alerts vs only quickpeek to measure downstream adoption.
- Auto-suggest incident runbook steps based on matched filter patterns (seeded by solutions engineering).
- ML-powered root-cause hints (longer-term) that combine traces + logs + metrics.

Next steps for grooming session (owner: Asha):
- 1) Sync with backend (Kenji) to validate aggregation feasibility and latency (this week).
- 2) Quick UX sketch review with Jordan and Marta (add accessibility notes) (3 days).
- 3) Split tickets for sprint planning; estimate story points and move to backlog.

Notes to self:
- Keep the card lean — it should be a decision shortcut, not a full analysis surface.
- Avoid over-automation: filters should be suggested, not auto-applied.
- Ask sales for a shortlist of customers for early testing (especially those with high alert churn).

References & inspiration:
- internal: trace-compact-cards experiment (confluence link in linked_artifacts), alert-sidecar prototype from 2024 hackathon.
- external: Lightstep / Honeycomb compact trace preview screenshots for pattern cues.

End of doc.
